original_value: SummaryNetwork environments are becoming increasingly complex, making traffic monitoring and security analysis more difficult. To address unstable detection accuracy and the burden of centralized processing, this study proposes an adaptive traffic anomaly filtering framework for distributed intrusion detection systems. By combining support vector machine classification with edge computing, the method performs localized feature screening and model selection to reduce communication delay and improve response time. Experiments show that the approach can lower false alarms, support encrypted traffic recognition, and decrease workload on the central server while maintaining reliable classification performance.

result.paraphrase: As network environments grow more complex, traffic monitoring and security analysis become increasingly difficult. To address unstable detection accuracy and the strain of centralized processing, this study presents an adaptive traffic anomaly filtering framework for distributed intrusion detection systems. Combining support vector machine classification with edge computing, it carries out localized feature screening and model selection to cut communication delay and speed up response time. Experiments indicate that the method can reduce false alarms, recognize encrypted traffic, and lessen the central server’s workload while preserving reliable classification performance.
